Explain in your own words what 'DNA as the Genetic Material' refers to.
questions.a: Three classic experiments crowned DNA as the hereditary molecule: Griffith's 1928 heat-killed smooth pneumococci passed a 'transforming principle' to harmless rough cells, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty wiped the principle out only with DNase, and Hershey and Chase watched radioactive phosphorus - not sulfur-labelled protein - ride into E. coli inside T2 phages.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'DNA as the Genetic Material'.
questions.a: Whoever destroys DNA destroys the transforming ability, and only the phage's DNA enters the host - so DNA, not protein, carries heredity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'DNA as the Genetic Material' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Gene Packaging in Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gene Packaging in Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes' refers to.
questions.a: Bacteria squeeze one circular chromosome into a nucleoid by negative supercoiling helped by histone-like proteins, while eukaryotes wind linear DNA around histone octamers of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4 into beads-on-string nucleosomes with a single H1 holding the linker, then coil 10 nm fibres through 30 nm and 300 nm stages to 700 nm metaphase chromosomes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gene Packaging in Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes'.
questions.a: Supercoiling packs the bacterial loop; histone spools and progressive folding tuck metres of eukaryotic DNA into a nucleus.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gene Packaging in Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Semi-Conservative Replication Machinery' refers to.
questions.a: Each daughter duplex keeps one parental strand and gains one new complement - the semi-conservative rule that Messelson and Stahl proved with heavy nitrogen and caesium chloride gradients; helicase unzips the fork, primase lays 10-12 nucleotide RNA primers, DNA polymerase III extends only 5' to 3', the lagging side is built in 1000-2000 nucleotide Okazaki pieces, polymerase I swaps primers for DNA, and ligase seals the nicks.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Semi-Conservative Replication Machinery'.
questions.a: One old strand plus one new strand per duplex, a continuous leading side and a discontinuous lagging side make replication semi-discontinuous.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Semi-Conservative Replication Machinery' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Transcription, mRNA Processing and Translation' refers to.
questions.a: RNA polymerase reads a promoter with its Pribnow box, unwinds about seventeen base pairs and strings ribonucleotides at roughly forty per second until a terminator - with sigma leaving after initiation and rho sometimes ending the run; eukaryotic transcripts then gain a methyl-G cap and a poly-A tail and lose their introns by splicing, before ribosomes translate the message codon by codon from charged tRNAs until a release factor meets a stop codon.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transcription, mRNA Processing and Translation'.
questions.a: Copy only the gene into RNA, dress and trim the eukaryotic transcript, then let tRNAs and the wobble rule translate it at the ribosome.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transcription, mRNA Processing and Translation' taught, and from which source text?
